old: It squeezes the Earth from all sides like a giant ball.
new: Every part gets pulled toward the middle. That makes a round ball.
reason: Gravity pulls toward the centre; 'squeezes from all sides' is loose

old: The water goes up into the air like a tiny mist.
new: The water gets too tiny to see. It floats up into the air.
reason: Water vapour is an invisible gas; mist is visible droplets

old: Plants and trees make it, and so do tiny plants in the sea.
new: Plants and trees make it, and so do tiny sea life.
reason: Many ocean phytoplankton are algae or bacteria, not plants

old: Jupiter has nearly a hundred moons that we know of.
new: Jupiter has more than ninety moons that we know of.
reason: Moon count keeps rising; 'more than ninety' stays true

old: A good throw skips a few times. The world record is 88 skips!
new: A good throw skips a few times. The record is nearly ninety!
reason: 88 skips verified (Kurt Steiner, 2013, Guinness); wording avoids going stale
